[(p-٢٢١)] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Ar-Ra'd (The Thunder)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see; then He established Himself over the Throne.﴾

The apparent meaning of this noble verse may suggest that the heaven is raised upon pillars, but we do not see them. A similar verse is His saying at the beginning of Surah Luqman: ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you can see, and He cast into the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you﴾ [Luqman: 10].

The scholars differed concerning His saying "that you can see" on two views:

The first: that the heavens have pillars, but we do not see them, as the apparent meaning of the verse indicates. Among those narrated from as holding this view are Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others, as stated by Ibn Kathir.

It is also narrated from Qatadah that the meaning is that they are raised without any pillars at all. This is the view of Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah. This view is indicated by Allah's explicit statement in Surah al-Hajj that it is He who holds the heaven from falling upon the earth, in His saying: ﴿And He holds back the heaven from falling upon the earth except by His permission﴾ [al-Hajj: 65].

Ibn Kathir said: According to this view, His saying "that you can see" is an emphasis on the negation of that, meaning: it is raised without pillars, just as you see it so; and this is the most perfect display of power. End of quotation.

The one who annotates this work, may Allah pardon him, says: The apparent meaning is that this statement belongs to the category of the negative proposition (al-salibah, a proposition that denies a predicate of a subject), which does not require the existence of the subject (al-mawdu', the subject). The intended meaning is the negation of the predicate's attribution to the subject, and this is true in two forms:

The first: that the subject exists, but the predicate is denied of it, as when you say: "Man is not a stone." Man exists, and stoneness is denied of him.

The second: that the subject does not exist, so it is understood that the judgment of that existential matter is negated from it. This type is among the styles of the Arabic language, as we have clarified in our book *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Inconsistency from the Verses of the Book). Its example in the language is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*Over a faint track whose landmarks offer no guidance,
when the Nabataean camel, sniffing at it, bellowed.*

(p-٢٢٢) That is, there is no landmark on it at all by which one could be guided. And his saying:

*Its terrors do not startle the hare,
nor does one see the lizard burrowing in it.*

That is: there are no hares in it and no lizards.

Based on this, His saying ﴿without pillars that you can see﴾ means: there are no pillars for it that you could see. The word 'amad (pillars) is the plural of 'amud (pillar) by irregular formation (not following the regular pattern). Among its uses is the saying of Nabighah Dhubyani:

*And subdue the jinn; I have indeed permitted them
to build Tadmur with smooth stones and pillars.*

Al-Suffah, with a damma and shaddah, is a broad stone.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 13, Verse 6**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the evil before the good, though exemplary punishments have already passed before them﴾, and so on.

Here, "the evil" (al-sayyi'ah) means punishment and the sending down of torment. "Before the good" means before well-being and before faith. In this verse, God has made clear that the disbelievers ask the Prophet (ﷺ) to hasten for them the punishment with which he warns them if they persist in disbelief. He has explained this meaning in many verses:

• As in His saying: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment, but God will not fail His promise﴾ [al-Hajj: 47].

• And His saying: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment. Were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them, and it will surely come upon them suddenly while they are unaware﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 53].

• And His saying: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 54].

• And His saying: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1, 2].

• And His saying: ﴿And when they said, "O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky"﴾, and the verse [al-Anfal: 32].

And His saying: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [al-Shura: 18]; and His saying: ﴿And they said, "Our Lord, hasten for us our portion before the Day of Reckoning"﴾ [Sad: 16]; and other verses besides these.

The cause of their asking for the punishment to be hastened is obstinacy and their claim that the Prophet (ﷺ) is lying about the punishment and retribution of God with which he warns them, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them until a counted nation, they will surely say, "What is holding it back?"﴾ [Hud: 8]. And like His saying: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel, and they defied the command of their Lord, and said, "O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the messengers"﴾ [al-A'raf: 77]; and His saying: ﴿They said, "O Nuh, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation, so bring us what you threaten us with, if you are of the truthful"﴾ [Hud: 32]. This point has already been indicated earlier.

"Al-mathulat" means the punishments; its singular is "mathlah."

The meaning is: they ask for the punishment to be hastened out of rebellion and transgression, and they did not take warning from what God inflicted upon the earlier nations of exemplary punishments, that is, the penalties, as He did to the people of Nuh, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, the people of Lut, the people of Shu'ayb, Pharaoh and his people, and others.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing, and indeed your Lord is severe in punishment﴾.

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, has made clear that He is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing, and that He is severe in punishment. Thus He combined promise and threat, so that people's hope in His grace may be great, and their fear of His punishment and His severe torment may be intense. This is because the aspirations of intelligent people are confined to attracting benefit and warding off harm, so the combination of fear and hope is more conducive to obedience. This meaning has been explained in many verses:

• As in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So if they deny you, say, "Your Lord is the possessor of vast mercy, but His punishment will not be turned away from the criminal people"﴾ [al-An'am: 147].

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾ [al-An'am: 165 and al-A'raf: 167 in the source's citation].

• And His saying, majestic and exalted: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful. And that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ [al-Hijr: 49, 50].

And His saying: ﴿Forgiver of sin and Acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty﴾ [Ghafir: 3], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You are only a warner﴾, meaning: your duty is only to deliver the message and to warn. As for their guidance and their success, that is in the hand of God, exalted is He, just as their reckoning is with Him, exalted is He.

This meaning is clarified in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but God guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:272], His saying: ﴿Upon you is only the delivery of the message, and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:40], and similar verses.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾.

The most apparent of the opinions regarding this noble verse is that the "people" (qawm) means the community (ummah), and the "guide" (hadi) means the Messenger, as is indicated by His saying: ﴿And for every community there is a messenger﴾ [Yunus 10:47], and His saying: ﴿And there has been no community but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir 35:24], and His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent into every community a messenger﴾ [al-Nahl 16:36]. We have explained the opinions of the scholars and their evidences concerning this noble verse in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" (Removing the Illusion of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book).

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-310) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Ra'd (the chapter of Thunder).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide﴾.

This noble verse explicitly states that for every people there is a guide. However, other verses indicate that some peoples had no guide, whether we interpret guidance in its specific meaning or its general meaning. Among the verses indicating that some people had no guide in the specific sense, is His saying: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you﴾ [al-An'am 6:116]. These misleaders were not guided by a guide in the specific guidance, which is divine success toward what pleases God. A parallel to it is His saying: ﴿But most people do not believe﴾ [Hud 11:17], and His saying: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you strive, will not be believers﴾ [Yusuf 12:103], and His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:8], and others besides these verses.

Among the verses indicating that some peoples had no guide in the general sense, which is clarifying the path, is His saying: ﴿That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:6], based on the verification that "mā" here is negative (nāfiyah), not relative (mawsulah). And His saying: ﴿O People of the Scripture, there has certainly come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you after a interval [of messengers]﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:19].

Those who died during this interval had no guide in the more general sense either.

The answer to this is from four aspects:

The first: the meaning of His saying ﴿and for every people there is a guide﴾ is: a caller who calls them and guides them, either to good, like the prophets, or to evil, like the devils. That is, you, O Messenger of God, are a warner and a guide to every good. This view is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas through 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah. It has also occurred in the Qur'an that guidance is used for guiding to evil, as in:

• His saying: ﴿It is decreed for him that whoever takes him as an ally, he will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾ (p-311) [al-Hajj 22:4],

• His saying: ﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat 37:23],

• His saying: ﴿Nor to guide them to a path except the path of Hell﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:168]. As also occurs in the Qur'an, the use of "imam" for one who calls to evil, in His saying: ﴿And We made them imams calling to the Fire﴾ [al-Qasas 28:41].

The second: the meaning of the verse is: You, O Muhammad ﷺ, are a warner, and I am the guide of every people. This is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas through al-'Awfi, and from Muhammad, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and others, as Ibn Kathir said.

According to this view, His saying ﴿and for every people there is a guide﴾ refers to Himself, exalted is He. A parallel to it in the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿And none informs you like one who is aware﴾ [Fatir 35:14], meaning Himself, as Qatadah said. A parallel to it from the speech of the Arabs is the saying of Qatadah ibn Salamah al-Hanafi:

"And if I live, I will surely set out on a raid that gains spoils, or a noble one will die."

Meaning himself.

The clarification of this topic will come, God willing, in the surah "al-Qari'ah". The meaning according to this view is: You, O Muhammad, are a warner, and I am the guide of every people whom happiness and guidance preceded in My knowledge. This is due to the evidence of many verses that He guided some peoples and misled others, in accordance with what His eternal knowledge had predetermined, such as His saying: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed God does not guide one whom He misguides﴾ [al-Nahl 16:37].

The third: the meaning of ﴿and for every people there is a guide﴾ is: a leader (qa'id). The leader is the imam, and the imam is the deed. This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah, as Ibn Kathir transmitted from him.

According to this view, the meaning is: and for every people there is a deed that guides them to what they are heading toward, of good or evil. The meaning of this aspect is supported by His saying: ﴿There every soul will know (tabluu) what it has sent forward﴾ [Yunus 10:30], according to the reading of one who reads it with two taa's (tatlū), meaning: every soul will follow what it sent forward of good and evil.

As for the view that the meaning of "tatlū" is: it reads in its record of deeds what it has done of good and evil, (p-312) then there is no evidence in the verse. It is also supported by the hadith: "Let every community follow what it used to worship. So whoever used to worship the sun will follow the sun, whoever used to worship the moon will follow the moon, and whoever used to worship the idols (tawaghit) will follow the idols," and so on.

The fourth: this was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd: the "people" means the community, and the "guide" means the prophet. So the meaning of His saying ﴿and for every people there is a guide﴾ is: for every community there is a prophet, like His saying: ﴿And there has been no community but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir 35:24], and His saying: ﴿And for every community there is a messenger﴾ [Yunus 10:47].

The Qur'an often uses the term "qawm" (people) for the community (ummah), as in:

• His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people﴾ [Hud 11:25],

• His saying: ﴿And to 'Ad, their brother Hud, he said: O my people﴾ [al-A'raf 7:65],

• His saying: ﴿And to Thamud, their brother Salih, he said: O my people﴾ [al-A'raf 7:73],

and similar.

According to this view, the meaning of "qawm" in His saying ﴿and for every people there is a guide﴾ is more general than whatever the term "qawm" linguistically applies to. What clarifies this is the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah al-Qushayri, may God be pleased with him, in the Sunan and the Musnad collections: "You will complete seventy communities," and so on.

It is known that what the term "qawm" linguistically applies to is more than seventy times over. The conclusion of this fourth view is that the verse is like His saying: ﴿And there has been no community but that a warner has passed among them﴾, and His saying: ﴿And for every community there is a messenger﴾, and there is no difficulty in this, because the communities are limited to seventy, as the hadith explains. So the forefathers of the people who were not warned, mentioned for example in His saying: ﴿That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:6], are not an independent community, such that the problem of their not being warned would arise alongside His saying: "And there has been no community but that a warner has passed among them." Rather, they are part of a community. And His saying: ﴿And there has been no community but that a warner has passed among them﴾ is not confused by His saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would have sent into every town a warner﴾ [al-Furqan 25:51], because the meaning is: We sent to all the towns, indeed to the black and the red (of mankind) a single messenger, who is Muhammad ﷺ. Yet if We had willed, We would have sent to each town separately a messenger. But We did not do so, so that sending to all people would manifest his superiority over other messengers, by giving him what no one before him among the messengers was given, peace and blessings be upon him and upon them.

As is established from him ﷺ in the Sahih (authentic collection), that the universality of his message to the black and the red is among the things God specifically gave him, not given to other messengers.

(p-313) The closest of the mentioned views to us, the one indicated by the Glorious Qur'an, is the fourth view, namely that the meaning of the verse ﴿and for every people there is a guide﴾ is: for every community there is a prophet. So, O Prophet of God, you are not an innovation among the messengers.

The way the Qur'an indicates this is the frequent occurrence of similar statements in verses:

• such as His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent into every community a messenger, [saying]: Worship God and avoid the false gods (taghut)﴾ [al-Nahl 16:36],

• and His saying: ﴿And for every community there is a messenger﴾,

• and His saying: ﴿And there has been no community but that a warner has passed among them﴾.

Accordingly, the wisdom in informing that for every community there is a prophet is that the polytheists were astonished at his ﷺ being sent to them, as He explained:

• in His saying: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man from among them: Warn the people?﴾ [Yunus 10:2],

• and His saying: ﴿Rather, they wondered that a warner came to them from among themselves﴾ [Qaf 50:2],

• and His saying: ﴿And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said: Has God sent a human as a messenger?﴾. So He informed them that his warning to them is neither a wonder nor a strange thing, because every community has a warner. The verse is thus

• like His saying: ﴿Say: I am not an innovation among the messengers﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:9],

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:163].

And God, exalted is He, knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (*Adwa' al-Bayan*) on surah 13, verse 8 (part 1 of 3):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah knows what every female carries﴾.

The word *ma* (what) in this verse may be a relative pronoun (*mawsulah*) with a deleted returning pronoun, meaning: "He knows that which every female carries." On this reading the meaning is: He knows what she carries of offspring, in whatever state it is, whether male or female, whether it is an incomplete birth (*khida'*), whether beautiful or ugly, tall or short, blessed or wretched, and other conditions besides these.

Verses of the Book of Allah indicate this meaning, such as His saying: ﴿And He knows what is in the wombs﴾ [Luqman: 34], since *ma* there is undisputedly a relative pronoun. Also His saying: ﴿He knows you best, since He produced you from the earth and when you were embryos in the wombs of your mothers﴾ [al-Najm: 32], and His saying: ﴿He it is who shapes you in the wombs however He wills﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 6].

It may also be that the word *ma* in the noble verse is a verbal-noun particle (*masdariyyah*), meaning: He knows the carrying of every female in the verbal sense. Verses have also come indicating this meaning, such as His saying: ﴿No female carries or gives birth except with His knowledge, and no one is granted a long life or has his life shortened except that it is in a Book﴾ [Fatir: 11], and His saying: ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour. No fruit comes out of its sheaths, and no female carries or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾ [Fussilat: 47].

We have already stated in the introduction to this blessed book that a verse may have two aspects, both of which are correct and both of which are supported by the Qur'an, so we mention them all.

As for the possibility that the word *ma* in this verse is interrogative, it is, as it appears to me, far-fetched, even though some scholars have held it. The authentic Sunnah has shown that the knowledge of what is in the wombs, as stated in the mentioned verses, is among the things Allah has reserved for Himself apart from His creation. This is what is established in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, that the intended meaning of the "keys of the unseen" in His saying: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ [al-An'am: 59], are the five mentioned in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ [Luqman: 34]. The two possible meanings of the word *ma* in His saying ﴿knows what carries﴾ [al-Ra'd: 8] also apply to His saying: ﴿And what the wombs diminish and what they increase﴾ [al-Ra'd: 8]. So if *ma* is a relative pronoun in both, the meaning is: He knows that which they diminish and that which they increase; and if it is a verbal-noun particle, the meaning is: He knows their diminishing and their increasing.

The scholars differed regarding the intended meaning of His saying: ﴿And what the wombs diminish and what they increase﴾ [al-Ra'd: 8]. These are their views on the verse, through the transmission of the author of *al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bil-Ma'thur* (The Scattered Pearls in Tafsir by Transmission):

Ibn Jarir reported from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying ﴿And what the wombs diminish and what they increase﴾, he said: "It is the woman who sees blood during her pregnancy."

(p-225) Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And what the wombs diminish﴾, he said: "The flow of blood." And "what they increase," he said: "Its retention."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning His saying: ﴿And what the wombs diminish﴾, he said: "That she sees blood during her pregnancy." And "what they increase," he said: "In the nine months."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported, through the route of al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning His saying: ﴿And what the wombs diminish and what they increase﴾, he said: "What they increase beyond nine and what they decrease from nine."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: ﴿And what the wombs diminish﴾, he said: "What is less than nine months. And what they increase beyond nine."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning His saying: ﴿And what the wombs diminish﴾, meaning: "the miscarriage." And "what they increase," he says: "What it increased in pregnancy beyond what it diminished, until she gives birth to it complete. This is because some women carry for ten months, some carry for nine months, some increase in pregnancy and some decrease. That is the diminishing and the increase that Allah the Exalted mentioned, and all of that is by His knowledge, exalted is He."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from al-Dahhak, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "What is less than nine months is diminishing, and what is beyond it is increase."

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh reported from 'Ikrimah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Whenever the womb diminished by blood for a day, it increased in pregnancy by a day, until it completed nine months, pure."

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning His saying: ﴿And what the wombs diminish﴾, he said: "The miscarriage." Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Mujahid, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the verse, who said: "When she sees blood, the child becomes frail, and when she does not see blood, the child grows large." (End of quote) from *al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bil-Ma'thur*.

(p-226) It has been said: the diminishing and the increase refer to the child itself, such as the loss of a finger or other part, and the addition of a finger or other part.

It has been said: the diminishing is the cessation of menstrual blood, and what they increase is the postnatal bleeding (*nifas*) after delivery.

al-Qurtubi mentioned these two views.

It has been said: "diminish" means it contains one child, and "increase" means it contains twins or more.

The one who annotates this, may Allah pardon him, says: The reference of all these views is to one thing, which is that He, the Exalted, knows what the wombs diminish and what they increase. This is because "diminish" means "reduce," and "increase" means "take in excess." So it includes the mentioned reduction: reduction in number, reduction of a limb of the fetus, reduction of its body when she menstruates while carrying, so that it shrinks; and reduction of the duration of pregnancy, by miscarrying it before the usual term of gestation. Just as increase includes: increase of a limb, increase of number, increase of the body of the fetus if she does not menstruate while pregnant, and increase of the term of pregnancy beyond the usual measure. Allah, exalted and majestic, knows all of that, and the verse includes all of it.

A Note

Some scholars have derived from this noble verse that the minimum and maximum duration of pregnancy, and the minimum and maximum duration of menstruation, are matters of *ijtihad* (independent reasoning), since Allah has reserved the knowledge of that for Himself, as in His saying: ﴿Allah knows what every female carries and what the wombs diminish﴾, and so on.

No ruling may be issued regarding any of that except to the extent that Allah has made it apparent to us, and that which is found apparent among women, whether rare or customary. We will mention, if Allah wills, the views of the scholars on the minimum and maximum of pregnancy and the minimum and maximum of menstruation, and we will prefer what appears to be the stronger by evidence.

So we say, and in Allah the Exalted we seek help:

Know that the scholars have agreed that the minimum duration of pregnancy is six months. The Qur'an's indication of this will come, since His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And his carrying and his weaning is thirty months﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15], when you add to it His saying: ﴿and his weaning is in two years﴾ [Luqman: 14], there remains from the thirty months, after the weaning period, six months for the duration of pregnancy. This indicates that it is a term of pregnancy in which the fetus is born complete, as its clarification will come, if Allah wills, exalted is He.

'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan was born after six months. These six months are reckoned by lunar months, like all the months of the Sharia, due to His saying: ﴿They ask you about the crescents. Say: They are timings for people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 189], the verse.

al-Qurtubi said: "For this reason it has been narrated in the school of Malik, from some of Malik's companions, and I think it is in the book of Ibn Harith, that if it falls short of the six months by three days, the child is attributed to the father, due to the reason of the variation in the length of months. Ibn 'Atiyyah narrated it." (End of quote.)

The one who annotates this, may Allah pardon him, says: What appears, and Allah the Exalted knows best, is that a counted month is taken from its beginning as it is, whether full or deficient, and that a broken (incomplete) month is completed as thirty days. As for the maximum duration of pregnancy, nothing has been specified regarding its limit in the Book or the Sunnah, and the scholars differ about it, and each of them speaks according to what has appeared to him of the conditions of women.

Imam Ahmad and al-Shafi'i held that the maximum duration of pregnancy is four years, which is one of the two well-known narrations from Malik. The other well-known narration from Malik is five years. Imam Abu Hanifah held that its maximum is two years, which is a narration from Ahmad, and it is the view of al-Thawri, and 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, also said so. From al-Layth: three years. From al-Zuhri: six and seven. From Muhammad ibn al-Hakam: one year and no more. From Dawud: nine months.

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: "This is an issue for which there is no basis except independent reasoning and reference to what is known of the affairs of women." al-Qurtubi said: "al-Daraqutni reported, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, who said: I said to Malik ibn Anas: I have been told, from 'A'ishah, that she said: A woman does not extend her pregnancy beyond two years, the length of the shadow of a spindle. He said: Glory be to Allah! Who says this?! This is our neighbour, the wife of Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan. She carries and gives birth in four years, and she was called 'the carrier of the elephant'."

It is also narrated: One day Malik ibn Dinar was sitting when a man came to him and said: "O Abu Yahya, pray for my wife, who has been pregnant for four years! She has become in severe distress." Malik became angry and closed the Mushaf, then said:

"These people think we are only prophets," then he recited, then he supplicated, then he said: "O Allah, if there is wind in this woman's belly, expel it from her, and if there is a girl in her belly, change her into a boy, for You erase and establish, and with You is the Mother of the Book." Malik raised his hand and the people raised their hands. The messenger went to the man and said: "Go to your wife." The man went, and Malik did not lower his hand until the man came out of the door of the mosque with a curly-haired boy on his neck, four years old, whose teeth had come in and whose navel cord had not been cut.

It is also narrated: A man came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "O Commander of the Believers, I was absent from my wife for two years, then I came and she was pregnant." 'Umar consulted the people about stoning her. Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Commander of the Believers, if you have authority over her, you have no authority over what is in her belly. Leave her until she gives birth." So he left her, and she gave birth to a boy whose front teeth had come out. The man recognized the resemblance and said: "My son, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" 'Umar said: "The women have failed to bear the likes of Mu'adh. Had it not been for Mu'adh, 'Umar would have perished."

al-Dahhak said: "My mother bore me, and she had carried me in her belly for two years, and she gave birth to me when my tooth had come out."

It is mentioned from Malik that he was carried in his mother's belly for two years, and it was said three years. It is said that Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan remained in his mother's belly for three years, and she died with him while he was violently moving, so her belly was split open and he was taken out with his teeth grown. Hammad ibn Salamah said: Hahram ibn Hayyan was only named Harim because he remained in his mother's belly for four years.

al-Ghaznawi mentioned that al-Dahhak was born after two years with his tooth already come out, so he was named Dahhak (the one who laughs).

From 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam, who said: "A neighbour of ours gave birth after four years to a boy whose hair reached his shoulders. A bird passed by him, and he said to it: 'Kash!'" (End of the words of al-Qurtubi.)

The one who annotates this, may Allah pardon him, says: The view with the strongest evidence is that there is no limit for the maximum duration of pregnancy, and this is the third narration from Malik, as al-Qurtubi transmitted it from him. This is because every limitation to a specific period has no basis and no evidence for it, and limiting a period without a sound source is clearly baseless. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 8 (part 2 of 3):

As for the minimum and maximum of menstruation (hayd), the scholars have also differed concerning it. Malik held that the minimum of menstruation, with regard to worship such as fasting and the obligation of ghusl, has no limit. Rather, if a single drop of blood came from a woman, it would be a menstrual period (hayda) with regard to worship. As for with regard to istibra' (waiting period to establish the womb is clear) and 'idda, it has been said that it is likewise. The well-known view is that the amount of this is referred to women who have knowledge of it, by the measure that indicates the womb's being clear of menstruation. Khalil ibn Ishaq said in his Mukhtasar, in which he stated what the fatwa is based on: "The amount of menstruation here is referred to [women]: whether it is a day or part of it..." up to his saying "lil-nisa'" (to women), meaning: the whole of that is referred to women. End of quote.

It is apparent that for Malik this falls under tahqiq al-manat (determining the operative cause), and women know best about the operative cause in this matter.

As for the maximum of menstruation according to Malik, it is, with regard to the first menstrual period in which a woman had not menstruated before: half a month. If the blood continues beyond half a month, she is then a mustahadah (woman with irregular bleeding). As for a woman who is accustomed to menstruation, the maximum duration of her menstruation according to him is the addition of three days as a precaution (istizhar) over the longest of the times of her habit, if the length of her menstruation varies. So if she menstruated six days one time, five days another time, and seven days another time, she takes three days as a precaution over the seven days, because it is the maximum of her habit. The application of this is when that does not exceed half a month. If it exceeds half a month, then she is pure upon the passing of half a month. All of this concerns a woman other than a pregnant one, and the discussion of this topic, God willing, will come concerning the blood that a pregnant woman sees.

This is the summary of Malik's school regarding the minimum and maximum of menstruation. As for the maximum of purity (tuhr), there is no limit to it, and there is no disagreement among the scholars on this. As for the minimum of purity in Malik's school, Malik did not state it explicitly. Rather, he said: women are asked about the number of days of purity.

Shaykh Abu Muhammad said in his Risala: it is about eight days or ten days. Ibn Siraj said: "It is fitting that the fatwa be based on this," because Shaykh Abu Muhammad inferred this from the Mudawwana, and it is the view of Sahnun. Ibn Maslama said: "The minimum of purity in Malik's school is fifteen days," and the author of al-Talqin relied on it, and Ibn Shas made it the well-known view, and Khalil ibn Ishaq followed it in his Mukhtasar, where he said: "And its maximum for one who is beginning is half a month, like the minimum of purity."

Imam al-Shafi'i and Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on them both, in the sound well-known view from them both, held that the minimum of menstruation is a day and a night, and its maximum is fifteen days. This is the view of 'Ata' and Abu Thawr. The minimum of purity according to al-Shafi'i, by the agreement of his companions, is fifteen days. Al-Mawardi reported from most of the people of knowledge that the minimum of purity is fifteen days. al-Thawri said: the minimum of purity between two menstrual periods is fifteen days.

Abu Thawr said: "This is among the things on which they do not differ, to our knowledge."

Imam Ahmad held that the minimum of purity between two menstrual periods is thirteen days. al-Athram and Abu Talib narrated this from him. We have mentioned many times that there is no limit to the maximum of purity by consensus. al-Nawawi said in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab: "The evidence for the consensus is induction (istiqra'), because that is existent and observed. Among the most remarkable of it is what al-Qadi Abu al-Tayyib reported in his Ta'liq, he said: 'A woman informed me about her sister that she menstruates one day and night every year, and she is healthy, conceives and gives birth, and her postpartum bleeding (nifas) is forty days.'"

Imam Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, held that the minimum of menstruation is three days, and its maximum is ten. It is reported from Abu Yusuf: its minimum is two days and the maximum of the third. The minimum of purity according to Abu Hanifa and his companions is fifteen days, and there is no limit to its maximum according to him, as we have mentioned several times the reporting of consensus on it. Excepted from this is the consideration of the accustomed mustahadah for the times of her purity and her menstruation.

And from Yahya ibn Aktham: the minimum of purity is nineteen days. al-Mawardi reported from Malik three (p-230) narrations concerning the maximum of menstruation: the first: fifteen; the second: seventeen; the third: unlimited.

From Makhul: the maximum of menstruation is seven days. From Abd al-Malik ibn al-Majishun: the minimum of purity is five days. It is reported about the women of al-Majishun that they used to menstruate seventeen [days]. Ahmad said: "The most we have heard of is seventeen."

This is the summary of the scholars' views on the minimum and maximum of menstruation, and these are their evidences. As for Abu Hanifa and whoever agreed with him, they argued for their view that the minimum of menstruation is three and its maximum is ten by the hadith of Wathila ibn al-Asqa', may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "The minimum of menstruation is three days and its maximum is ten days."

And by what is reported from Abu Umama, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Menstruation does not exceed ten days nor fall below three days." And by what is reported from Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: "Menstruation is three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten," and they said: Anas would not say this except on the basis of revelation (tawqif). They said: Because this is a determination, and a determination is not valid except by revelation or consensus, and consensus has only been reached on three. The majority rejected the argument from the aforementioned hadiths on the ground that they are weak and cannot be established as proof by the like of them.

al-Nawawi said in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab, the text of which is: "As for the hadith of Wathila, Abu Umama, and Anas, all of them are weak, agreed upon as weak by the hadith scholars. al-Daraqutni clarified their weakness, then al-Bayhaqi in the Kitab al-Khilafiyyat, then in al-Sunan al-Kubra." End of quote.

Ibn Qudama said in al-Mughni: The hadith of Wathila is narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Shami, who is weak, from Hammad ibn al-Minhal, who is unknown. The hadith of Anas is narrated by al-Jald ibn Ayyub, who is weak. Ibn 'Uyayna said: it is a hadith with no basis. Ahmad said concerning the hadith of Anas: "It is nothing; this comes from al-Jald ibn Ayyub." It was said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated it; he said: "I do not think he heard it except from al-Hasan ibn Dinar," and he weakened it greatly. Yazid ibn Zurai' said: "Abu Hanifa only argued with al-Jald ibn Ayyub." The hadith of al-Jald is opposed by what was reported from Ali, may God be pleased with him, for he said: "What exceeds fifteen is istihada, and the minimum of menstruation is a day and a night." al-Bayhaqi said in al-Sunan al-Kubra: "This is a hadith known through al-Jald ibn Ayyub, and this has been denied against him." al-Bayhaqi also said: Ibn 'Ulayya said: "al-Jald is a Bedouin who does not know hadith." He also said: al-Shafi'i said: "You and I do not establish the like of the hadith of (p-231) al-Jald, and we rely on the error of one who is more reliable than him with less than this."

He also said: Sulayman ibn Harb said: Hammad, meaning Ibn Zayd, used to weaken al-Jald and say: "He did not understand hadith."

al-Bayhaqi also narrated with his chain from Hammad ibn Zayd, who said: "Jarir ibn Hazim and I went to al-Jald ibn Ayyub, and he narrated to us the hadith of Mu'awiya ibn Qurra from Anas concerning the menstruating woman. We went to check it, and he did not distinguish between the menstruating woman and the mustahada." He also narrated with his chain from Ahmad ibn Sa'id al-Darimi, who said: "I asked Abu Asim about al-Jald ibn Ayyub, and he weakened him greatly, and said: 'He was a shaykh among the shaykhs of the Arabs; our companions were lax in narrating from him.'" al-Bayhaqi also narrated from Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak that the people of Basra used to deny the hadith of al-Jald ibn Ayyub and say: "He is a shaykh among the shaykhs of the Arabs, not a man of hadith." Ibn al-Mubarak said: "The people of his own land know him better than others." Ya'qub said: "I heard Sulayman ibn Harb, Sadaqa ibn al-Fadl, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and it reached me from Ahmad ibn Hanbal that they used to weaken al-Jald ibn Ayyub and did not regard him as a place of proof." He also narrated with his chain from Ibn 'Uyayna that he used to say: "What is al-Jald? Who is al-Jald? Who was al-Jald?" He also narrated with his chain from Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who said: "I heard my father mention al-Jald ibn Ayyub, and he said: 'His hadith is not worth anything; he is weak in hadith.'" End of quote. We have extended the discussion on weakening this report only because it is the strongest thing that has come in this chapter despite its weakness, as you see. al-Bayhaqi said in al-Sunan al-Kubra: "Weak hadiths have been reported concerning the minimum and maximum of menstruation, the weakness of which I have clarified in al-Khilafiyyat."

As for the proof of those who say that the minimum of menstruation is a day and a night and its maximum is fifteen, like al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and those who agree with them, it is that no determination has been established from the Shari'a on this, so it is necessary to return to what is observed in existence, and what is observed is that menstruation is not less than a day and a night nor more than half a month. They said: It has been established by widespread transmission from the Salaf, from the Successors and those after them, that this exists as an observed fact. al-Bayhaqi and others narrated it from 'Ata', al-Hasan, Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, Yahya ibn Sa'id, Rabi'a, Sharik, al-Hasan ibn Salih, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, may God have mercy on them all.

al-Nawawi said: "If it is said: Ishaq ibn Rahawayh narrated from some of them that a woman of the women of al-Majishun menstruated twenty days, and from Maymun ibn Mihran that the daughter of Sa'id ibn Jubayr was under him and used to menstruate two months in the year, then the answer to it is what the author answered in his book al-Nukat: that these two reports are weak. (p-232) As for the first: it is from 'some of them,' who is unknown, and some of them denied it, and Imam Malik ibn Anas denied it, as did other scholars of Madina. The second: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated it from a man, from Maymun, and the man is unknown. And Allah knows best." End of quote.

As for the proof of Malik concerning the maximum of menstruation for the beginner, it is like the proof of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. His proof concerning its maximum for the accustomed woman is what Imam Malik, Ahmad, al-Shafi'i, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah narrated from Umm Salama, may God be pleased with her, that she "asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a woman who was bleeding blood, and he said: 'Let her look at the number of nights and days that she used to menstruate and their amount in the month, and let her leave prayer. Then let her perform ghusl and tighten a cloth (istithfar), and then pray.'" End of quote.

This hadith is explicit regarding the return to the habit of the menstruating woman.

Ibn Hajar said in al-Talkhis concerning this hadith: al-Nawawi said its chain is according to the conditions of both (Bukhari and Muslim). al-Bayhaqi said: "It is a well-known hadith, except that Sulayman ibn Yasar did not hear it from Umm Salama." In a narration of Abu Dawud, from Sulayman, a man informed him from Umm Salama. al-Mundhiri said: Sulayman did not hear it from her. Musa ibn Uqba narrated it from Nafi', from Sulayman, from Marjana, from her. al-Daraqutni traced it through Sakhr ibn Juwayra, from Nafi', from Sulayman, that a man narrated to him from her. End of quote.

There are many corroborating reports for the hadith that strengthen the return of women to their habit in menstruation, such as the hadith of Hamna bint Jahsh, and the hadith of 'A'isha in the story of Fatima bint Abi Hubaysh. As for the addition of three days, it is for the sake of precaution (istizhar) and careful assessment at the end of the menstrual period, and I know of no basis for it from the established texts of revelation. As for Malik's proof concerning the minimum of menstruation with regard to acts of worship, it is adherence to the apparent generality of the texts, and no sound text has been reported specifying a limit.

وأما أقلُّه بالنسبة إلى العدّة والاستبراء، فحجّته فيه أنه من قبيل **تحقيق المناط** (*tahqiq al-manat*، أي تطبيق الحكم الشرعي على محلّه المعيّن)، لأن الحيض دليلٌ عاديٌّ على براءة الرحم، فلا بدّ فيما طُلبت فيه البراءة بالحيض من دلالة على براءة الرحم بحيضٍ يدلّ على ذلك بحسب العادة المطّردة. ولذا جُعل الرجوع في ذلك إلى النساء العارفات بذلك، لأن تحقيق المناط يُرجع فيه لمن هو أعرف به، وإن كان لا حظّ له من علوم الوحي. وحجّة يحيى بن أكثم في قوله: «إن أقلّ الطُّهر تسعةَ عشرَ»، هي أنه يرى أن أكثر الحيض عشرةُ أيام، وأن الشهر يشتمل على طُهرٍ وحيض، فعشرةٌ منه للحيض والباقي (p-233) طُهرٌ، وقد يكون الشهر تسعةً وعشرين، فالباقي بعد عشرة الحيض تسعةَ عشرَ. وهذا هو حاصل أدلّتهم، وليس على شيءٍ منها دليلٌ من كتابٍ ولا سنّةٍ يجب الرجوع إليه. وأقربُ المذاهب في ذلك هو أكثرها موافقةً للمشاهَد، ككون الحيض لا يقلّ عن يومٍ وليلة ولا يكثر عن نصف شهر، وكون أقلّ الطُّهر نصفَ شهر، والله تعالى أعلم.
* *
**مسألة**
اختلف العلماء في الدم الذي تراه الحامل: هل هو حيض، أو دمُ فساد؟ فذهب مالك، والشافعي في أصحّ قوليه، إلى أنه حيض، وبه قال قتادة والليث، وروي عن الزهري، وإسحاق، وهو الصحيح عن عائشة. وذهب الإمام أبو حنيفة، والإمام أحمد، إلى أنه دمُ فسادٍ وعلّةٍ، وأن الحامل لا تحيض، وبه قال جمهور التابعين، منهم سعيد بن المسيّب، وعطاء، والحسن، وجابر بن زيد، وعكرمة، ومحمد بن المنكدر، والشعبي، ومكحول، وحمّاد، والثوري، والأوزاعي، وابن المنذر، وأبو عبيد، وأبو ثور.
واحتجّ من قال: إن الدم الذي تراه الحامل حيضٌ، بأنه دمٌ بصفات الحيض في زمن إمكانه، وبأنه مترددٌ بين كونه فساداً لعلّةٍ أو حيضاً، والأصل السلامة من العلّة، فيجب استصحاب الأصل.
واحتجّ من قال بأنه دمُ فساد بأدلّة، منها: ما جاء في بعض روايات حديث ابن عمر في طلاقه امرأته في الحيض، أن النبي ﷺ قال لعمر: «مُرْه فليراجعها ثم ليطلّقها طاهراً أو حاملاً». وهذه الرواية أخرجها أحمد، ومسلم، وأصحاب السنن الأربعة. قالوا: قد جعل ﷺ الحمل علامةً على عدم الحيض، كما جعل الطُّهر علامةً لذلك.
ومنها: حديث: «لا تُوطأ حاملٌ حتى تضع، ولا حائلٌ حتى تُستبرأ بحيضةٍ»، رواه أحمد، وأبو داود، والحاكم من حديث أبي سعيد رضي الله عنه، وصححه الحاكم، وله شواهد. قالوا: فجعل ﷺ الحيض علامةً على براءة الرحم، فدلّ ذلك على أنه لا يجتمع مع الحمل.
ومنها: أنه دمٌ في زمنٍ لا يُعتاد فيه الحيض غالباً، فكان غيرَ حيضٍ قياساً على ما تراه اليائسة، بجامع غلبة عدم الحيض في كلٍّ منهما.
وقد قال الإمام أحمد رحمه الله: «إنما يعرف النساءُ الحملَ بانقطاع الدم».
ومنها: أنه لو كان دمَ حيضٍ لما انتفت عنه لوازمُ الحيض، فلمّا انتفت عنه دلّ ذلك على أنه غيرُ حيض؛ لأن انتفاء اللازم يوجب انتفاء الملزوم. فمن لازم الحيض حرمةُ (p-234) الطلاق، ودمُ الحامل لا يمنع طلاقها، للحديث المذكور آنفاً الدالّ على إباحة طلاق الحامل والطاهر. ومن لازم الحيض أيضاً انقضاءُ العدّة به، ودمُ الحامل لا أثر له في انقضاء عدّتها، لأنها تعتدّ بوضع حملها، لقوله تعالى: ﴿وَأُولَاتُ الْأَحْمَالِ أَجَلُهُنَّ أَن يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ﴾ [الطلاق: ٤]. وفي هذه الأدلة مناقشاتٌ ذكر بعضها النوويُّ في شرح المهذّب.
واعلم أن مذهب مالك التفصيلُ في أكثر حيض الحامل، فإن رأته في شهرها الثالث إلى انتهاء الخامس تركت الصلاة نصفَ شهرٍ ونحوَه، وفسّروا «نحوَه» بزيادة خمسة أيام، فتجلس عشرين يوماً. فإن حاضت في شهرها السادس فما بعده تركت الصلاة عشرين يوماً ونحوَها، وفسّروا «نحوَها» بزيادة خمسة أيام، فتجلس خمساً وعشرين، وفسّره بعضهم بزيادة عشرة، فتجلس شهراً. فإن حاضت الحامل قبل الدخول في الشهر الثالث، فقيل: حكمُه حكمُ الحيض في الثالث، وقد تقدّم.
وقيل: حكمُه حكمُ حيض غير الحامل، فتجلس قدرَ عادتها وثلاثةَ أيام استظهاراً.
وإلى هذه المسألة أشار خليلُ بن إسحاق المالكي في مختصره بقوله: «ولحاملٍ بعد ثلاثةِ أشهرٍ النصفُ ونحوُه، وفي ستةٍ فأكثرَ عشرونَ يوماً ونحوُها، وهل ما قبل الثلاثة كما بعدها أو كالمعتاد؟ قولان».
هذا هو حاصل كلام العلماء في أقلّ الحيض وأكثره، وأقلّ الطُّهر وأكثره، وأدلّتهم في ذلك، ومسائل الحيض كثيرةٌ، وقد بسط العلماء الكلام عليها في كتب الفروع.
* *
**مسألة**
اختلف العلماء في أقلّ النفاس وأكثره أيضاً، فذهب مالك، والشافعي، إلى أن أكثره ستون يوماً، وبه قال عطاء، والأوزاعي، والشعبي، وعبيد الله بن الحسن العنبري، والحجاج بن أرطاة، وأبو ثور، وداود. وعن ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن أنه قال: أدركتُ الناسَ يقولون: أكثر النفاس ستون يوماً. وذهب الإمام أبو حنيفة وأحمد إلى أن أكثره أربعون يوماً، وعليه أكثر العلماء. قال أبو عيسى الترمذي: أجمع أهل العلم من أصحاب النبي ﷺ ومَن بعدهم على أن النفساء تدع الصلاة أربعين يوماً إلا أن ترى الطُّهر قبل ذلك، فتغتسل وتصلّي. اهـ.
قال الخطّابي: وقال أبو عبيد: وعلى هذا جماعةُ الناس. وحكاه ابن المنذر عن عمر بن الخطاب، وابن عباس، وأنس، وعثمان بن أبي العاص، وعائذ بن عمرو، وأم سلمة، وابن (p-235) المبارك، وإسحاق، وأبي عبيد. اهـ.
وحكى الترمذي، وابن المنذر، وابن جرير، وغيرهم، عن الحسن البصري أنه خمسون. وروي عن الليث أنه قال: قال بعض الناس: إنه سبعون يوماً. وذكر ابن المنذر، عن الأوزاعي، عن أهل دمشق: أن أكثر النفاس من الغلام ثلاثون يوماً، ومن الجارية أربعون. وعن الضحاك: أكثره أربعة عشر يوماً. قاله النوويّ.
وأما أقلّ النفاس فهو عند مالك، والشافعي، وأحمد، وأبي حنيفة في أصحّ الروايات عنه، لا حدّ له، وهو قول جمهور العلماء. وعن أبي حنيفة: أقلّه أحدَ عشرَ يوماً، وعنه أيضاً: خمسةٌ وعشرون. وحكى الماوردي، عن الثوري: أقلّه ثلاثة أيام. وقال المزني: أقلّه أربعة أيام.
وأما أدلّة العلماء في أكثر النفاس وأقلّه، فإن حجّة كلّ من حدّد أكثره بغير الأربعين هي الاعتماد على المشاهَد في الخارج، وأكثر ما شاهدوه في الخارج ستون يوماً. وكذلك حججهم في أقلّه فهي أيضاً الاعتماد على المشاهَد في الخارج، وقد يُشاهَد الولد يخرج ولا دم معه، ولذا كان جمهور العلماء على أن أقلّه لا حدّ له. وأما حجّة من حدّده بأربعين، فهي ما رواه الإمام أحمد، وأبو داود، والترمذي، وابن ماجه، والدارقطني، والحاكم عن أم سلمة رضي الله عنها، قالت: «كانت النفساء على عهد رسول الله ﷺ تجلس أربعين يوماً» الحديث. رُوي هذا الحديث من طريق علي بن عبد الأعلى، عن أبي سهل، واسمه كثير بن زياد، عن مسّة الأزدية، عن أم سلمة. وعلي بن عبد الأعلى ثقة، وأبو سهل وثّقه البخاري وضعّفه ابن حبان، وقال ابن حجر: لم يصب في تضعيفه، وقال في «التقريب» في أبي سهل المذكور: ثقة، وقال في «التقريب» في مسّة المذكورة: مقبولة. وقال النوويّ في «شرح المهذّب» في حديث أم سلمة هذا: حديث حسن رواه أبو داود، والترمذي، وغيرهما.
قال الخطّابي: أثنى البخاري على هذا الحديث، ويعتضد هذا الحديث بأحاديث بمعناه من رواية أبي الدرداء، وأنس، ومعاذ، وعثمان بن أبي العاص، وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهم. وقال النوويّ أيضاً بعد هذا الكلام: «واعتمد أكثرُ أصحابنا جواباً آخرَ وهو تضعيفُ الحديث، وهذا الجواب مردود، بل الحديث جيّدٌ كما سبق».
وأجاب القائلون بأن أكثر النفاس ستون عن هذا الحديث الدالّ على أنه أربعون بأجوبة، أوجهُها عندي أن الحديث إنما يدل على أنها تجلس أربعين، ولا دلالة فيه على أن الدم إن تمادى بها لم تجلس أكثر من الأربعين، فمن الممكن أن تكون النساء المذكورة في الحديث لم يتمادَ الحيض بها إلا أربعين، فنصّ الحديث على أنها تجلس الأربعين، ولا (p-236) يُنافي أن الدم لو تمادى عليها أكثر من الأربعين لجلست أكثر من الأربعين. ويؤيّده أن الأوزاعيّ رحمه الله قال: «عندنا امرأةٌ ترى النفاسَ شهرين»، وذلك مشاهَدٌ كثيراً في النساء. والعلم عند الله تعالى.

The Qur'anic verse: ﴿It is the same for you, whether one of you conceals his speech or speaks aloud, and whether one hides by night or goes forth openly by day.﴾

He, may He be exalted, shows in this noble verse that secret speech and open speech are equal before Him, and that concealment and manifestness are also equal before Him. This is because He hears secret speech as He hears open speech, and knows the hidden as He knows the apparent. He has clarified this meaning in other verses, such as His saying: ﴿And keep your speech secret or declare it; indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.﴾ And His saying: ﴿And if you speak aloud, indeed He knows the secret and that which is more hidden.﴾ And His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, when they wrap themselves in their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.﴾ And His saying: ﴿And We have already created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him.﴾ And other verses besides these.

The more apparent of the two opinions regarding al-mustakhfi bil-layl (ٱلْمُسْتَخْفِي بِاللَّيْلِ, "the one who hides by night") and al-sarib bil-nahar (ٱلسَّارِبِ بِالنَّهَارِ, "the one who goes forth by day") is that al-mustakhfi is the one who conceals himself and is hidden from eyes, and al-sarib is the one who is manifest and conspicuous, going wherever he wishes. From this is the saying of al-Akhnas ibn Shihab al-Taghlibi:

*Every people have drawn close to the tether of their stallion, but we have loosed its tether, so it is a sarib (roaming free).*

That is: it goes wherever it wishes, openly, without concealment.

And the saying of Qays ibn al-Khatim:

*I have gone forth openly, though I was not one who goes forth openly, and dreams bring near what is not near.*

It is also said: al-sarib is the one who enters the sirb (a hiding place, a shelter) in order to be concealed in it, and al-mustakhfi is the one who is apparent, from *khafāhu yakhfīhi*, meaning "he made it apparent." From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*He brought them forth from their burrows as if the rain of an evening, pouring down, had brought them out.*

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 11:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah wills misfortune for a people, there is no repulsing it, and they have not besides Him any patron.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that He does not change the blessing and well-being of a people until they change what is in themselves of obedience to Allah, majestic and exalted is He.

The meaning is that He does not strip a people of a blessing He has bestowed upon them until they change what they were upon of obedience and righteous deeds. He clarified this meaning in other places, such as His saying: ﴿That is because Allah would not change a blessing He had bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves﴾ [al-Anfal: 53], and His saying: ﴿And whatever disaster strikes you is for what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [al-Shura: 30].

In this verse He has also made clear that when He wills a people harm, there is no repulsing it. He clarified this in other places as well, such as His saying: ﴿and His punishment is not turned back from the criminal people﴾ [al-An'am: 147], and similar verses. His saying in this noble verse, ﴿until they change what is in themselves﴾, is true even if the change is made by some of them, as happened on the day of Uhud when the archers changed what was in themselves, so the calamity afflicted everyone. He (ﷺ) was asked: "Will we be destroyed while righteous people are among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness becomes abundant." And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who shows you the lightning, [causing] fear and hope﴾ — the verse.

In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, mentions that He is the One who shows His creation the lightning, [causing] fear and hope. Qatadah said: "Fear" is for the traveler, who fears its harm and hardship, and "hope" is for the one who stays at home, who hopes for its blessing and benefit and hopes for the provision of Allah. And from al-Hasan: "Fear" is for the people of the sea, and "hope" is for the people of the land. And from al-Dahhak: "Fear" is of the thunderbolts, and "hope" is for the rain.

And He made clear in another place that His showing His creation the lightning, [causing] fear and hope, is among His signs, majestic and exalted, which indicate that He alone is deserving of being worshipped, with no partner. That is in His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning, [causing] fear and hope, and sends down water from the sky﴾ — the verse [ar-Rum: 24].

The Exalted said: ﴿And to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and their shadows [too] in the mornings and the evenings.﴾

In this noble verse, He the Exalted has made clear that the people of the heavens and the earth prostrate to Him, willingly and unwillingly, and their shadows prostrate to Him in the mornings and the evenings. He also mentioned the prostration of shadows and the prostration of the people of the heavens and the earth in His words: ﴿Have they not seen what things Allah has created, how their shadows incline to the right and the left, prostrating to Allah while they are humbled?﴾ and ﴿And to Allah prostrate whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels, and they are not arrogant﴾ [an-Nahl: 48, 49], up to His words ﴿and they are commanded﴾ [an-Nahl: 50].

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of the prostration of the shadow and the prostration of those who are not believers. Some scholars said: the prostration of "whoever is in the heavens and the earth" is of the general term that is specified (al-'amm al-makhsus). Thus the believers and the angels prostrate to Allah with a true prostration, which is placing the forehead on the ground, and they do this willingly; while the disbelievers prostrate unwillingly, meaning the hypocrites, because they are disbelievers inwardly and do not prostrate to Allah except unwillingly, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And when they stand up for prayer, they stand up lazily, showing off to the people﴾ up to the end of the verse [an-Nisa': 142], and He the Exalted said: ﴿And nothing prevented their contributions from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and they do not come to prayer except while lazy, and they do not spend except while they are unwilling﴾ [at-Tawbah: 54]. The evidence that the prostration of the people of the heavens and the earth is of the specified general term is His words in the Surah of al-Hajj: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures and many of the people? And many have deserved the punishment﴾ [al-Hajj: 18]. So His words ﴿and many of the people﴾ [al-Hajj: 18] are evidence that some people are not included in the mentioned prostration. This is the saying of al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others, and al-Farra' mentioned it. It was also said that the verse is general. The meaning of the prostration of the Muslims willingly is their submission to what Allah wills from them willingly, and the meaning of the prostration of the disbelievers unwillingly is their submission to what Allah wills from them unwillingly; because His will is effective in them, and they are subject and submissive to His creation in them and to the execution of His will in them. The original meaning of prostration in the Arabic language is humility and submission. From it is the saying of Zayd al-Khayl:

*With a host among whom the spotted horses lose their way in its chambers; you see the hills prostrating therein to the hooves.*

And from it is the saying of the Arabs: "asjada" (he prostrated) when he lowered his head and bowed. Humayd ibn Thawr said:

*When they twisted around a wrist and a palm dyed with henna and its bracelets,*
*the excess of its reins made it prostrate, a prostration like the Christians to their rabbis.*

According to this view, the prostration is linguistic, not legislative (shar'i). This disagreement also applies to the prostration of shadows. It was said: their prostration is real, and Allah the Exalted is able to create for them a perception by which they perceive and prostrate to Allah with a true prostration. It was also said: their prostration is their inclining by the power of Allah at the beginning of the day towards the west and at its end towards the east. Those who said this claimed that the shadow has no real existence, since it is an image, so perception is not possible from it.

We say: Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, is capable of all things, so He is able to create for the shadow a perception by which it prostrates to Allah the Exalted with a true prostration. The established principle among the scholars of usul (legal theory) is: the texts of revelation are to be taken according to their apparent meanings, except with evidence from the Book or the Sunnah. It is not hidden that the outcome of the two views is:

That one of them: the prostration is legislative, and according to it, it is in the case of the people of the heavens and the earth of the specified general term.

And the second: the prostration is linguistic, meaning submission, humility and lowliness, and according to it, it remains on its generality. The established principle in usul according to the Malikis, the Hanbalis and a group of the Shafi'is is that if a text is ambiguous between the legislative meaning (al-haqiqah al-shar'iyyah) and the linguistic meaning (al-haqiqah al-lughawiyyah), it is taken as the legislative, and this is the verified view, contrary to Abu Hanifah, who gives precedence to the linguistic meaning, and contrary to the one who says the word becomes mujmal (ambiguous) because it admits of both this and that. The author of "Maraqi al-Su'ud" framed this issue with his saying:

*The word is carried to the legislative meaning, if there is none then the general customary meaning.*

So the linguistic is upon the clear, and there is no need to investigate metaphor in what has been chosen.

It was also said: the meaning of the prostration of the disbelievers unwillingly is the prostration of their shadows unwillingly. It was also said: the verse concerns the believers, so some of them prostrate willingly, due to the ease of complying with the commands of the Law for them, and some prostrate unwillingly, due to the heaviness of the hardship of the obligation upon them, though their faith drives them to bear that effort. And Allah knows best.

His saying the Exalted: ﴿بِالغُدُوِّ﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 15] (bil-ghuduww, "in the mornings") may be a verbal noun (masdar), or it may be the plural of ghadah (morning). And al-Asal is the plural of uslun (with two dammas), which is the plural of asil, meaning what is between the afternoon prayer and sunset. From it is the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali:

*By my life, you are indeed the house, whose people I honour, and I sit in its shade in the evenings.*

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 27:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾

In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, makes clear that the disbelievers proposed to him (ﷺ) that he bring a sign which his Lord would send down upon him. He clarified this meaning in several places, such as His saying: ﴿So let him bring us a sign, as the former messengers were sent [with signs]﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:5], and beyond that of the verses. He, exalted is He, made clear in another place that the Noble Qur'an is sufficient as a substitute for all signs, in His saying: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:51]. And He clarified in another place the wisdom behind not sending down a sign such as the she-camel of Salih and the like, by His saying: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her﴾ [al-Isra' 17:59], as the allusion to it has already passed.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if only there were a Qur'an by which the mountains could be set in motion, or the earth could be split asunder, or the dead could be made to speak...﴾ (verse)

The answer (jawab) to "law" (if only / had it been) in this verse is omitted. Some scholars said its implied construction is: "this Qur'an would have been [the one that does it]" (lakana hadha al-Qur'an). Others said its implied construction is: "you would have disbelieved in the Most Merciful" (lakafartum bil-Rahman). The latter view is supported by His words before it: ﴿while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Ra'd: 30]. We have already presented examples of the omission of the answer of "law" in Surat al-Baqarah. We also presented in Surat Yusuf that the general rule in the Arabic language is that the omitted answer is of the same kind as what was mentioned before the condition (al-shart), so that what precedes the condition serves as evidence for the omitted answer.

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those to whom We have given the Book rejoice in what has been sent down to you﴾, and so on.

This noble verse, by its apparent meaning, indicates the faith of the People of the Book, because rejoicing in what was sent down to the Prophet is a sign of faith.

Similar to it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recitation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 121], and His saying: ﴿Say: "Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it..."﴾ and so on [al-Isra': 107].

However, there are verses that indicate otherwise, such as His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not to be separated...﴾ - up to His saying - ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 1-6]. In another place He clarified that the disbelievers among the People of the Book are more numerous, and that is His saying: ﴿And if the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110].

The answer is that the verse belongs to the general term that has been specified (al-'amm al-makhsus, a general expression restricted by a specifying indication). It refers specifically to the believers among the People of the Book, such as 'Abd Allah ibn Salam and those Jews who embraced Islam, and the well-known eighty from the Christians who embraced Islam, as stated by al-Mawardi and others. This is clear, and it is indicated by the partitive in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah﴾ and so on [Al 'Imran: 199].

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We had certainly sent messengers before you and made for them wives and descendants﴾, and so on, to the end of the verse.

In this noble verse He makes clear that the messengers before him (ﷺ) were of the kind of mankind: they married and had children, and they were not angels. The reason is that the disbelievers found it strange that a human being among mankind should be sent as a messenger. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human being as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra: 94]. So He informed that He sends human beings who marry and eat, as in His words: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ [al-Furqan: 20], and His words: ﴿And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾ [al-Anbiya: 8], and other verses besides these, as the reference to them has already passed.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 13, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book."﴾

The apparent meaning is that His saying "and whoever has knowledge of the Book" is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to the word "Allah" (lafẓ al-jalālah), and that what is meant by it is the people of knowledge of the Torah and the Gospel. This is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge [bear witness also]﴾, and His saying: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Book before you﴾ [al-Nahl: 43], and His saying: ﴿So ask the people of the reminder if you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 43], and other verses besides these.
